episodes.title: Born Into the FLDS: Nomz Bistline on Sam Bateman, Prison, and Finding Her Freedom
episodes.description: In this episode of the Get Obsessed podcast, Julie Lokun and Mika sit down with Naomi “Nomz” Bistline, who was raised in the FLDS and later appeared in the Netflix documentary Trust Me: The False Prophet, to talk about growing up in a high control society and how she reclaimed her own story. Naomi explains what the FLDS is, why she now sees it as a cult rather than a church, and how obedience, separation from family, and assigned relationships shaped her childhood. She describes being told at 19 that she belonged to Samuel Bateman, how his control wore down her sense of self, and why victims sometimes move closer to the person who poses the greatest threat. She also shares the events that led to her arrest, her nearly two years in pretrial detention, and her testimony against Sam. Naomi calls prison both the best and worst thing that ever happened to her. It gave her space to think for herself, to read over 300 books, and to discover music. The conversation closes with her life today, including psychology studies, songwriting, and her hope of building a music career. In this episode, we discuss: Growing up in the FLDS and how curiosity and imagination kept her going What the FLDS is and why Naomi views it as a cult How families were separated and how she came to be placed with a caretaker Being told at 19 that she belonged to Samuel Bateman Why victims can grow close to their abusers and how coercive control made her feel robotic The arrest, the time in pretrial detention, and testifying against Sam Why prison was both the best and worst thing to happen to her Finding freedom through books, music, and a guitar ABOUT THE GUEST: Naomi “Nomz” Bistline, who now goes by Nomzia, was born and raised in the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (FLDS), a polygamist sect that broke away from mainstream Mormonism. At 19, she was told she belonged to Samuel Bateman, a self-proclaimed prophet who claimed to be Warren Jeffs' heir, and she became one of his most loyal wives. She was released from prison on September 4, 2024. Since then, she has been studying psychology, writing music, and working in the fashion world, pursuing the things she was told she could never do. Naomi is the only one of Bateman's wives interviewed on camera for the Netflix documentary Trust Me: The False Prophet, released in 2026. She is now sharing her story in her own words and working toward a career in music. episodes.title: Beyond the Documentary: Dr. Christine Marie on Cults, Coercion, and Giving Voice (Part 2)
episodes.description: In this episode of the Get Obsessed podcast, Julie Lokun continues her conversation with Dr. Christine Marie, going behind the scenes of Trust Me The False Prophet and the years she spent building trust inside the FLDS community. Dr. Christine explains how vulnerability and the need to belong can make people susceptible to religious cults, how destructive groups can control thoughts, relationships, information, behavior, and emotions, and how she began recognizing troubling behavior surrounding Sam Bateman. She also shares what happened after recording evidence of abuse, the challenges of working with law enforcement, and the eventual investigation that led to Sam Bateman's arrest and 50-year sentence. The conversation also explores the impact on women and families, the importance of speaking up when someone is being harmed, and why survivors should have the freedom to tell their stories in their own time. In this episode, we discuss: How vulnerability and the need to belong can make people susceptible to cult control Cult control and its influence on thoughts, relationships, information, and behavior Early rumors about Sam Bateman and his relationships with underage girls A confession that revealed ritualistic sexual abuse within Sam's group The investigation, law enforcement challenges, and the events that led to Sam's arrest The lasting effects on women, children, and families connected to the community Why speaking up against harm matters and how survivors can reclaim their stories ABOUT THE GUEST: Dr. Christine Marie holds a PhD in Psychology specializing in media psychology, along with an MBA and a specialization in Positive Psychology. She is an author, speaker, researcher, educator, kindness advocate, and certified Trauma and Resiliency Life Coach. Her work focuses on coercive control, cult psychology, media trauma, public shaming, critical thinking, kindness, and resilience. In 2021, she received the Outstanding Dissertation Award from the American Psychological Association's Division of Media Psychology and Technology. Christine is the founder of Voices for Dignity, a nonprofit supporting marginalized communities and survivors. She has spent the past decade doing humanitarian and dignity work in Short Creek and has extensive experience working with members of the FLDS community. In 2026, she was featured in the Netflix documentary Trust Me: The False Prophet. episodes.title: Dr. Christine Marie of Trust Me: The False Prophet, Talks Inside the FLDS, Polygamy, and Building Trust (Part 1)
episodes.description: In this episode of the Get Obsessed podcast, Julie Lokun sits down with Dr. Christine Marie to unpack the story behind Trust Me The False Prophet and her years living in Short Creek, an FLDS community. Christine explains why she moved to Short Creek in 2016, how her own experiences with polygamy shaped her initial perspective, and how getting to know FLDS families challenged some of the assumptions she had formed through sensational media coverage. The conversation explores how cultic influence works, why Christine believes it is important to look at coercion rather than stereotypes, and how she and her husband Tolga gradually built trust within the community. She also discusses the role of media in giving people the opportunity to tell their own stories, the impact of Warren Jeffs remaining influential while imprisoned, and how Sam Bateman used that loyalty to establish his own authority. In this episode, we discuss: Moving to Short Creek and challenging assumptions about the FLDS through firsthand experience Christine's experience with polygamy and trauma and how it shaped her work with survivors Understanding cultic influence and coercive control through different forms of control Building trust within the FLDS community and connecting with people in Short Creek Using media to give people a voice and let FLDS members share their own stories Warren Jeffs and Sam Bateman's influence and Bateman's rise to authority Why people enter high control groups and how belonging and love bombing can lead to coercion ABOUT THE GUEST: Dr. Christine Marie holds a PhD in Psychology specializing in media psychology, along with an MBA and a specialization in Positive Psychology. She is an author, speaker, researcher, educator, kindness advocate, and certified Trauma and Resiliency Life Coach. Her work focuses on coercive control, cult psychology, media trauma, public shaming, critical thinking, kindness, and resilience. In 2021, she received the Outstanding Dissertation Award from the American Psychological Association's Division of Media Psychology and Technology. Christine is the founder of Voices for Dignity, a nonprofit supporting marginalized communities and survivors. She has spent the past decade doing humanitarian and dignity work in Short Creek and has extensive experience working with members of the FLDS community. In 2026, she was featured in the Netflix documentary Trust Me: The False Prophet.
